question: In △ABC, BD ⟂ AC at D and ∠DBC = 16°. E is a point on BC such that ∠CAE = 51°. What is the measure of ∠AEB?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In right-angled ▵BDC, the sum of the acute angles is exactly 90°.

⇒ ∠C = 90° − ∠DBC = 90° − 16° = 74°

By the Exterior Angle Theorem on ▵AEC, the exterior angle equals the sum of the remote interior angles.

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C

⇒ ∠AEB = 51° + 74° = 125°

**∴ The correct answer is 125°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ BD ⊥ AC at D in ▵ABC, which means ∠BDC = 90°.

⇒ ∠DBC = 16°

⇒ ∠CAE = 51°

**Step 1: Calculate ∠C using ▵BDC**

⇒ The sum of angles in any triangle is 180°.

⇒ In right-angled ▵BDC: ∠BDC + ∠DBC + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 90° + 16° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ 106° + ∠C = 180°

⇒ ∠C = 180° − 106° = 74°

**Step 2: Find ∠AEB using ▵AEC**

⇒ Since E is a point on BC, the line segment extends from C through E to B.

⇒ This makes ∠AEB an exterior angle to ▵AEC at vertex E.

⇒ According to the exterior angle theorem: ∠AEB = ∠CAE + ∠C

⇒ ∠AEB = 51° + 74°

⇒ ∠AEB = 125°

**∴ The correct answer is 125°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is perfectly equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles. (Formula: ∠Ext = ∠A + ∠B)

Triangle Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles in any standard triangle in Euclidean geometry is always exactly 180°.

Altitudes & Right Triangles

An altitude is a line drawn from a vertex meeting the opposite side at exactly 90°. It splits the main triangle into smaller right-angled triangles, enabling quick angle evaluations since the remaining two acute angles must sum to 90°.
